records.central_bank: Banco Central de la Republica Dominicana
records.category: central bank accumulated deficit carried as a state contingent liability
records.people: Camara de Cuentas de la Republica Dominicana (members not named on the page)
records.summary: In its report on the financial statements of the Dominican central government and the consolidated statements, reported by Diario Libre on 4 May 2023, the Camara de Cuentas de la Republica Dominicana recorded contingent liabilities of 664,333 millones de pesos, of which 94.05 per cent is the Banco Central's accumulated deficit of 624,824 millones, a figure that has tripled since 31 December 2005 when the accumulated losses recognised under Ley 167-07 stood at 202,141 millones.
records.detail: The same report flagged a 120,897 millones disagreement between the Ministry of Hacienda's Sigef and SIAB systems on acquisitions and valuations, 26,304 millones in assets not recorded in Sigef, cost differences of 100,759 millones, misclassified items in the central government cash flow statement, and receivables lacking required documentation. The subject of the finding is the central government's accounts and the Ministry of Hacienda; the Banco Central appears as the counterparty whose deficit the State carries off its own balance sheet, so counterparty_only is true and this does not colour the row. The page gives the delivery of the report only as este martes and no calendar date for that event, so no tabling date is asserted here; 4 May 2023 is the article's own publication date. The page writes Banco Central Dominicano rather than the bank's full legal name. This rests on press reporting of the Camara de Cuentas report, not on the report itself, which this round could not reach. Distinct from the Malkun and Calvo charges the map already holds for the Dominican Republic.
records.source_title: Camara de Cuentas senala inconsistencias en estados financieros, Diario Libre, 4 May 2023
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 72. The Camara de Cuentas finding is a QUANTIFICATION, not a case: it records contingent liabilities of 664,333 millones de pesos of which 94.05 per cent is the Banco Central's accumulated deficit of 624,824 millones, tripled since 2005. No conduct is alleged, no person or body is found at fault, and the observation is about the disclosure of the STATE's financial statements. That is the Finland test -- a figure with no episode -- and the Moldova test from round 71, where a compliance-positive audit was kept as a negative rather than filed as a case. An accumulated deficit is a balance-sheet magnitude, not corruption. REVERSES ON: a Camara de Cuentas finding against the Banco Central or its officials for conduct.

records.kind: the governor's property blocked by a foreign authority
records.summary: A United States Office of Foreign Assets Control notice published in the Federal Register of 7 March 2024 records that Executive Order 13288 of 6 March 2003, Executive Order 13391 of 22 November 2005 and Executive Order 13469 of 25 July 2008, all blocking the property of persons undermining democratic processes or institutions in Zimbabwe, were revoked effective 4 March 2024, and that the persons listed were therefore no longer subject to the blocking provisions and were removed from the Specially Designated Nationals List. Entry 8 of that list of removals is 'GONO, Gideon; DOB 29 Nov 1959; Passport AD000854 (Zimbabwe); Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (individual) [ZIMBABWE]', so the sitting governor of the central bank had been designated in that official capacity under the Zimbabwe orders and his property blocked by a foreign state until that date. The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe as an institution is not named in the notice; the person designated is its governor, identified by his central bank post rather than by private conduct. Zimbabwe's one existing record on this row is the 2009 public-pressure episode. The date in this record is the revocation date the notice gives; the notice does not state when Gono was first designated, so no designation date is asserted here.
records.quote: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe (individual)
records.source_title: Notice of OFAC Actions, Federal Register Vol. 89, No. 46, 7 March 2024 (Zimbabwe orders revoked effective 4 March 2024; SDN removals)
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 72, and the reason is that the record is INVERTED. Its kind says the governor's property was blocked by a foreign authority and its date is 2024-03-04 -- but the cited Federal Register notice of 7 March 2024 records that the three Executive Orders were REVOKED effective 4 March 2024 and that the listed persons were therefore no longer blocked. The source documents the END of the blocking, so the record dates an imposition to the day it was lifted. Separately, the underlying designation was of an individual, which this row excludes unless the act is against him as governor or against the bank. REVERSES ON: the original designation notice naming the Governor or the Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe, with its own date.

records.kind: the state's assets at central banks frozen by order of a regional bloc
records.summary: Anadolu Agency reports that at an extraordinary summit of West African leaders in Accra, Ghana, ECOWAS decided on the freezing of assets of the Republic of Mali in ECOWAS central banks and the freezing of assets of the Malian state and of state enterprises and parastatals in commercial banks, and suspended Mali from all financial assistance and transactions with regional financial institutions, over the delayed return to civilian rule. The page does not name the BCEAO, the central bank that issues Mali's currency, and refers only to 'ECOWAS central banks', so no finding about the BCEAO by name is asserted here. The date is the Sunday the article, published 10 January 2022, says the summit decided; the article does not print the calendar date 9 January 2022, which is read from that Sunday together with the publication date. Mali's single existing record on this row is the BCEAO union record of 22 January 2011 expanded into every member, so this is the first measure aimed at Mali itself. Filed with the caveat that the object of the freeze is the state's money held at central banks rather than the issuing bank's own reserves.
records.source_title: Anadolu Agency, 'ECOWAS imposes further sanctions on Mali', 10 January 2022
records.refused_reason: REFUSED at round 72 on the counterparty test. ECOWAS froze the assets of the REPUBLIC of Mali held in ECOWAS central banks, together with state enterprises' balances in commercial banks. The object is the state's money and the bank is its custodian, not the subject -- which is the Denmark shape the row already refuses, where the bank acting as the state's debt manager is not the bank being acted against. Mali is a BCEAO member with no central bank of its own, so a record keyed to MLI about Malian state deposits at the union bank would assert a move against a bank that is not Mali's. The source is also trade press and its date comes from 'Sunday' plus a publication date. REVERSES ON: an act against the BCEAO's own reserves, which would be keyed to the union and would need its own decision, or an act against Mali's national directorate of the BCEAO.
